Thank you for sharing your concerns, and we appreciate your openness in providing feedback about your experience with our practice. Your perspective is essential to us, and we take your comments seriously.

We want to assure you that we have actively engaged not only with your concerns but also with those of our other patients. Your feedback has prompted us to review our processes and communication channels. Since your review, we have been working diligently to make improvements, and we hope you have witnessed positive changes.

We acknowledge the importance of patient representation and the need for a collaborative approach. Your suggestion of a small committee of patients to provide feedback to the doctors is warranted although we already have a very successful PPG which you or any of our patients are welcome to join.

It's disheartening to hear that you feel the practice sends a message of disregard for patient opinions. We want to emphasise that your opinion is invaluable, and patient input is crucial in shaping our services. We are committed to fostering an environment where patients feel heard and respected.

Moving forward, we encourage you to continue voicing your concerns and opinions. We believe that working together and creating an open dialogue between patients and our team is vital for fostering a positive healthcare experience. Only through your feedback can we truly understand where improvements are needed and make the necessary changes.

We appreciate your understanding of the pressures faced by both doctors and patients. Our goal is to find a balance that ensures the best possible care and experience for everyone involved. If you have further thoughts or would like to discuss your concerns in more detail, please feel free to reach out to our patient advisors.

Thank you for being an advocate for positive change, and we look forward to working together to enhance our practice.

Kind regards,
Mr Christopher Hayhurst
Assistant practice manger

Mr C Hayhurst

Kind regards,
Mr C Hayhurst

am nearly 70 years old and visited the surgery on the morning of 24 December as my cold symptoms were getting worse. I had not slept for several nights due to a persistent cough and sore throat.
I was seen by a nurse who I understand was acting as a GP. She examined me briefly and said my throat was very red but that my chest was not infected. Obviously the majority of receptionists that dealt with me lacked experiance to be able to sort out what was needed in my care even though they had all my corispondence from Christie’s to guide them.

Thank you for taking the time to share your experience, and we're truly sorry to hear about the distressing symptoms you experienced. We completely understand how frightening an allergic reaction can be, and we're glad to hear you were able to receive the appropriate care promptly at the Urgent Treatment Centre.
At Ashton Medical Group, while we do offer some urgent appointments each day, these are not limitless and must be carefully prioritised based on clinical need. It's important to note that we are not an urgent care service and, in situations where symptoms may be potentially serious, such as breathing difficulties or suspected allergic reactions, our team is trained to signpost patients to more immediate services like the Walk in Centre or A&E, where more rapid assessments can be made.

We are pleased to see that our team directed you to the appropriate service to ensure you received timely medical attention. The safety and wellbeing of our patients is always our top priority, even if that means referring you to an alternative service that can better support your immediate needs.

If you require a follow-up with your GP regarding medication reviews or allergy screening, please don’t hesitate to contact us directly or submit an online consultation so we can arrange this for you as soon as possible.

Thank you again for your feedback, we take all concerns seriously and will use your comments to continue reviewing and improving our service.

Kind regards,
Mr C Hayhurst
Assistant Practice Manager My concern about the form is that the process for requesting a GP appointment is far from obvious. I have made a note of the sequence which I keep available. Without this I would probably give up!
The sequence of key strokes starts with Home. You then have to scroll to Upcoming & Past Appointments’. But this is not what is wanted or expected. There should be a link to ‘Request a new GP appointment’. Then the system says ‘No appointments available to book online’. Again misleading and some people will give up at this point.  Then ‘Ask your GP for medical advice’. Once again not clear.
This entire process makes complicated what should be simple. Accurx have asked for feedback. Please convey this back to them. A simplification of the process is badly needed.
Dr David Greenbaum",null,[0,198]]]],[null,1746690330000000,1746690330000000,"10 months ago",null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],"https://business.google.com/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/11279161296033722538/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZLYVZaMFRucGFlamwxUWpoM1JSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,["en"],[["Dear Dr Greenbaum,
Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback regarding the NHS App and the process for requesting a GP appointment. We completely understand your concerns, the current navigation can indeed be confusing, particularly for those unfamiliar with the system.

Your detailed observations are very helpful. The fact that you’ve had to create your own step-by-step guide to access services clearly highlights an area in need of improvement. We agree that the process should be far more intuitive, with a direct and clear option to "Request a new GP appointment" rather than navigating through less obvious menus.

We will ensure your comments are passed on to Accurx and NHS Digital, who are responsible for the app’s functionality and design. Feedback like yours plays a vital role in shaping future improvements to make access to care simpler and more patient-friendly.

In the meantime, if you or others require help with using the app or accessing services, please don’t hesitate to contact our reception team or drop in, we’d be happy to guide you.

What on earth are they doing at this outfit?

Thank you for sharing your recent experience, and we sincerely apologise for any inconvenience you encountered during your visit. Your feedback is invaluable, and we appreciate your patience.

We understand the frustration surrounding the confusion with your appointment location and the unnecessary wait. Since your review, we have been actively addressing these issues to enhance our communication processes and streamline patient experiences.

It's important to note that our GPs have been continually busy, having seen and dealt with over 6000 patients just last month. Despite the challenges, we recognise the need for more efficient processes and better communication.

We are taking steps to improve appointment details, ensuring clearer instructions for patients. Additionally, we are working on faster and more straightforward methods for discussing test results to minimize any unnecessary waits.
If you have any further concerns or wish to discuss your experience in more detail, please contact one of our patient advisors or use our website. We genuinely hope that since writing this review, you have observed positive changes in our practice.

Thank you for bringing these issues to our attention, and we value your understanding and ongoing support.

The ibuprofen suggested at the consultation was also high risk for my dad as it would seriously increase his risk of stroke. GPs are prescribing without using proper safety controls such as reviewing the patient's notes.

I left angry and frustrated.  My dad left distressed.
